text:
elaine: Quick FYI from customer onboarding call — the mix of env vars we document is inconsistent across SDK READMEs. People don't know whether to set REDWOOD_API_KEY or REDWOOD_ORG_KEY or both.

mike: oh no. we intentionally left "org vs project" vague to avoid scaring folks, but that's backfiring. What did they do?

elaine: they created a project token, exported REDWOOD_API_KEY with the org token still set in `~/.redwood/credentials`, and then `rw dev` processes kept hitting org-level quotas. Support asked why project-scoped limits didn't apply.

dave: that's the classic precedence confusion. Current behaviors: Node SDK -> env, file, metadata. Python SDK -> file, env, metadata. CLI -> cli-config, env, file. Yikes.

sophia: We need a small "scoping contract" and a short environment variable cheat-sheet in every SDK README. Also a predictable precedence rule: env > file > metadata > last-used. Keep "last-used" only for interactive suggestions, not resolution.

mike: agree. Also propose adding two optional helpers: 1) REDWOOD_PREFERS_PROJECT=true — if set, SDK will prefer project-scoped tokens when REDWOOD_PROJECT is set; 2) REDWOOD_DEBUG_AUTH=1 prints masked key id and lookup order. Both opt-in so we don't break existing users.

elaine: opt-in feels safe. But we should also make `rw auth rotate` emit a one-liner: "rotated project token proj_**** — current process will pick it up if REDWOOD_PREFERS_PROJECT=1 or after a shell restart". Clear expectations.

dave: we should also add a non-breaking server change: when a request fails due to scope mismatch, return structured error in body like `{"error":"scope_mismatch","attempted_key_id":"proj_****"}` but only expose masked id. That'll make support triage faster without leaking secrets. File a backend issue.

sophia: for docs: add a tiny diag table showing four combos (env set/unset x file present/absent) and what resolves. Example snippet: 
```
# prefer project when REDWOOD_PREFERS_PROJECT=1
export REDWOOD_PROJECT=team-a
export REDWOOD_PREFERS_PROJECT=1
export REDWOOD_API_KEY=proj_ABC
```
Also show how to check resolved key with `REDWOOD_DEBUG_AUTH=1 node sample.js`.

mike: tests: add integration matrix to CI that sets env vars and a fake `~/.redwood/credentials` and asserts which key ID the SDK reports. Put it behind a feature-flag job so it doesn't slow default CI.

elaine: I'll draft the docs PR and a sample-app patch. Mike, can you prototype the REDWOOD_PREFERS_PROJECT flag and the debug printing? Dave, can you open the backend ticket for scope_mismatch payloads and the support-safe mask rules?

dave: on it. I'll propose masked-id format `proj_****` and a privacy review.

sophia: small UX note: when clients fall back to org key while REDWOOD_PROJECT is set, add a visible warning once per process: "Warning: using org key while REDWOOD_PROJECT=team-a — run `rw auth use --project team-a` to switch". Make that silenced unless DEBUG or interactive.

devex-bot: Reminder: any change to auth resolution must include a changelog entry and migration guidance. Also please add tests covering the new feature flag behavior.

elaine: timeline: I'll open docs PR today, mike will open prototype PR tomorrow with tests, dave will file backend ticket. We'll circle back in next standup. Thanks! :raised_hands:
